pharm: Estrogen - hormonal contraceptive / hormone therapy component
quick: As contraceptive component: typically 20-35 mcg daily, combined with a progestogen
Take at the same time each day, with or without food
CONTRAINDICATED - not to be used in known or suspected pregnancy
Avoid in early breastfeeding - estrogen may reduce milk supply
Caution; not primarily renally cleared but monitor in significant impairment
Contraindicated in active liver disease / hepatic tumours
Blood pressure, VTE symptoms; lipids/glucose as indicated; breast and pelvic checks
summary: Ethinyl estradiol is the synthetic estrogen used as the estrogen component of almost all combined hormonal contraceptives and in some hormone therapy. Its ethinyl group resists first-pass metabolism, making it potent and orally active. Combined with a progestogen it suppresses ovulation and provides reliable contraception, and it helps cycle control. The principal serious risk is venous and arterial thromboembolism (raised by smoking, age over 35, obesity, migraine with aura and thrombophilia); it is contraindicated in pregnancy and in active liver disease. Note: in the US ethinyl estradiol is marketed only within combination products; this record describes the estrogen component (EMA/SmPC and BNF based).
indications: Estrogen component of combined hormonal contraceptives (with a progestogen) for prevention of pregnancy
Cycle control / management of menstrual disorders within combined preparations
Treatment of moderate acne and (in some preparations) hirsutism, as part of a combined product
Hormone replacement / hypoestrogenic states in selected formulations

dosage.d: 20-35 mcg ethinyl estradiol once daily with a progestogen
dosage.n: 21 active days then 7-day break, or per the specific 24/4 or continuous regimen
Lower estrogen dose to reduce estrogenic side effects

dosage.d: 30-35 mcg once daily with an appropriate progestogen
dosage.n: Per specific product (e.g. with cyproterone or drospirenone)

admin: Take one tablet at the same time every day to maintain efficacy
Follow the specific pill regimen (21/7, 24/4 or continuous) exactly
Start as directed (first day of period or per quick-start guidance) and use backup contraception when advised
If vomiting or severe diarrhoea occurs within a few hours of a dose, treat as a missed dose
Do not smoke - smoking greatly increases cardiovascular risk, especially over age 35
moa: Ethinyl estradiol binds estrogen receptors and, in combined contraceptives, works with the progestogen to suppress hypothalamic-pituitary release of FSH and LH, preventing follicular development and ovulation. It also stabilises the endometrium for good cycle control and raises sex-hormone-binding globulin. The 17-alpha-ethinyl group blocks oxidative metabolism, giving high oral potency.

absolute: Current or past venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE) or known thrombophilia
Arterial thromboembolic disease (MI, stroke, angina) or high arterial risk
Active liver disease, hepatic tumours, or severe hepatic impairment
Known or suspected estrogen-dependent cancer (e.g. breast cancer)
Smokers over 35 years (for combined contraceptive use)
monitor: Breast and cervical screening as appropriate

preg: CONTRAINDICATED. Estrogens are not indicated in pregnancy; if pregnancy occurs while taking it, stop the medicine. Inadvertent early-pregnancy exposure to combined contraceptives has not been clearly linked to birth defects, but use must cease.
lact: Avoid, particularly while establishing breastfeeding. Estrogens can reduce the quantity and quality of breast milk and small amounts pass into milk; progestogen-only or non-hormonal methods are preferred during lactation.
renal: Not primarily eliminated by the kidneys; no specific dose adjustment is defined, but use with caution in significant renal impairment and monitor blood pressure and fluid status.
hepatic: Contraindicated in active liver disease, severe hepatic impairment, cholestatic disorders and hepatic tumours, because estrogen is hepatically metabolised and can worsen cholestasis and stimulate hepatic adenomas. Stop if jaundice or significant liver enzyme rise occurs.

major: Enzyme-inducing drugs - rifampicin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, St John's wort, some HIV/HCV protease inhibitors (reduce contraceptive efficacy - use additional/alternative contraception)
Ulipristal acetate / certain hepatitis C regimens with ombitasvir (raised ALT - contraindicated combinations)
Lamotrigine (estrogen lowers lamotrigine levels - reduced seizure control)
moderate: Some antibiotics in individuals with altered enterohepatic recycling (caution advised by some guidelines)
Drugs raising potassium when combined with drospirenone-containing products
minor: Ascorbic acid and paracetamol (may modestly raise ethinyl estradiol)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; grapefruit juice may modestly raise levels
interactions.diagnostics: Alters thyroid (raises TBG/total T4), cortisol-binding globulin, clotting factors, triglycerides and other plasma proteins - interpret tests accordingly

serious: Arterial events - myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke
emergency: Suspected pulmonary embolism or DVT (chest pain, breathlessness, calf swelling)
Severe abdominal pain (possible hepatic or mesenteric event)
Sudden severe headache or visual loss

monitoring: Blood pressure at baseline and periodically
Assessment of VTE/arterial risk factors before and during use
Breast and cervical screening per local guidance
Lipids and glucose where clinically indicated
counsel: Take your pill at the same time every day for best protection
Do not smoke - it greatly raises the risk of clots and heart problems, especially over 35
Seek urgent help for leg swelling/pain, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, or sudden visual changes
Tell any prescriber you take this if starting new medicines (some reduce its effectiveness)
Follow the missed-pill instructions in your pack and use backup protection when advised
pk: Ovulation suppression established over the first cycle of correct use
Plasma peak approximately 1-2 hours after an oral dose
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light
pearls: In the US, ethinyl estradiol is available only as a component of combination products (with a progestogen); this record describes the estrogen component using EMA/SmPC and BNF sources
The 17-alpha-ethinyl group resists first-pass metabolism, giving high oral potency compared with natural estradiol
Venous and arterial thromboembolism is the key serious risk - screen for and counsel on risk factors (smoking, age >35, obesity, migraine with aura, thrombophilia)
Enzyme-inducing drugs (rifampicin, several antiepileptics, St John's wort) reduce contraceptive efficacy - additional contraception needed
Lowers lamotrigine levels and alters thyroid/cortisol binding globulins - relevant to seizure control and lab interpretation
missed: Follow the missed-pill rules for your specific product. In general, if one active pill is late by under 24 hours, take it as soon as you remember and continue normally; if missed by more than 24 hours or two or more are missed, take the most recent missed pill now, continue the pack, and use additional contraception (e.g. condoms) for 7 days - consider emergency contraception if intercourse occurred. Do not take more than two active pills in one day beyond making up the most recent miss.
overdose: Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, breast tenderness, fluid retention and, in females, withdrawal bleeding; serious toxicity is uncommon even after large ingestions, including in children. Management is supportive and symptomatic; there is no specific antidote.
